name: Tacet-Void
geological_features: Heavily cratered surface with no signs of geological activity
Regolith layer of uniform depth across the entire surface
Exposed bedrock in the oldest crater floors
specific_features: The Silence — an electromagnetic dead zone where even spacecraft instruments experience unexplained signal loss
A perfectly circular crater at the south pole whose origin remains debated
resources: Iron-nickel meteorite fragments on the surface
Pristine bedrock samples for geological dating
description: Tacet-Void is a tiny, dead world at the extreme outer edge of its star system, so far from any significant gravitational or electromagnetic influence that it exists in near-perfect isolation. The surface is a uniform blanket of ancient regolith over cratered bedrock, with no signs of geological activity for billions of years. It is, in every measurable sense, a world where nothing happens.

The absence of atmosphere means absolute silence, and the distance from its star means near-absolute darkness for much of its orbit. But the most unsettling feature is the electromagnetic dead zone — a region centered on the south polar crater where radio signals, sensor readings, and even some electronic equipment experience inexplicable degradation. The effect has no known physical explanation.

The south polar crater is the subject of ongoing investigation. Its geometry is too perfectly circular for a natural impact, yet there are no other signs of artificial construction. Some researchers have proposed it as a relic of ancient alien engineering, while others insist it falls within natural statistical variation for impact geometry. The electromagnetic anomaly associated with it resists all conventional explanation.

Tacet-Void's remoteness and the electromagnetic anomaly make it a destination for only the most dedicated researchers and the most curious explorers. The journey is long and the reward uncertain — a small, dark, silent world with one genuinely inexplicable feature. For some, that is enough. A semi-permanent research camp operates during the brief perihelion approach, when solar power becomes marginally viable, but for most of its orbit, Tacet-Void is truly alone.
